messages:
Marta Chen: FYI we started seeing decode drift on long-context runs after enabling FP8 KV in the staging cluster this morning. Not every model, but reproducible on 13B-ish variants with long prefix.
Alex Rivera: ugh, can you paste a minimal repro? batch size, tokens, and the kernel selection logs would help.
Marta Chen: repro is a low-batch (1-2 requests), long prefix ~12k tokens, decode length ~1k. We were using fp8-kv + fp8-decode kernels via the automatic kernel selector. Here's a trimmed trace from the runtime log:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:34Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=fp8_gemm_kv, seq_len=12288, batch=1, hw=A100
[2026-03-17T09:12:34Z] kv_quant: mode=per_channel, scale_table=auto_calib_v2, dtype=FP8
[2026-03-17T09:12:34Z] decode: step=512, tok_ms=18.3, kv_lookup_ms=4.7, kernel_ms=10.2
[2026-03-17T09:12:34Z] quality_check: perplexity_delta=+0.43 vs baseline_fp32
```
Marta Chen: quality issues = occasional token substitutions and weird punctuation insertion after long prefixes.
Pranay Gupta: interesting. Do we see it only when batch is small? Our batching heuristics prefer single-request fast-path for low latency, which disables some aggregation that helps numeric stability.
Marta Chen: looks like it. If I force minibatch=8 in the worker pool the issue mitigates, but latency increases.
Alex Rivera: can you run the profiling with kernel fallback to int8-kv and fp32-decode (force kernel selection override)? Want to see if the nondeterminism is from quantized KV accumulation or from FP8 GEMM on decode.
Rachel Li: I ran a quick A/B on a dev node: FP8 KV + FP8 decode = 18.3 ms/token, INT8 KV + FP8 decode = 19.1 ms/token, INT8 KV + FP32 decode = 22.9 ms/token. Quality-wise INT8 KV improved over FP8 in this case (less drift) but memory went up ~6% due to different packing.
perf-bot: profile summary uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/kvcache/jitter/1832045678/profiles.zip
Pranay Gupta: ok, two plausible hypotheses: 1) fp8 scale-table auto-calib for KV is underfitting high-dynamic long prefixes leading to truncation downstream, 2) small batches cause frequent kernel switches and mixed-precision accumulation inconsistencies.
Alex Rivera: Also consider the KV cache eviction/compact path: when sequence grows we do chunked copy into a contiguous buffer. If chunk copy uses fp8 ops and the scale is recomputed per-chunk that's another source.
Marta Chen: I instrumented kv write path and found a per-chunk scale recompute call. Snip:
```
for each chunk:
  scale = compute_scale(chunk); // uses running_abs_max heuristic
  quantized = quantize_fp8(chunk, scale)
  append_to_kv(quantized, scale)
```
Marta Chen: that running_abs_max was calibrated on shorter contexts during our offline calibrations. Long sequences have heavier tails.
Rachel Li: can we try two quick mitigations: a) use global scale per-request (compute on whole prefix) for KV writes, b) increase batch hint threshold so batching groups more requests when context > 8k.
Pranay Gupta: I can prototype (a) quickly. Risk: global scale needs an extra pass over the prefix which might add cost but probably cheaper than quality regression.
Alex Rivera: if we do (a) we should also change kernel selection fallback to prefer fp32-decode when global_scale_variance > threshold. That would be a small heuristic: if scale variance across layers > 0.2 then don't use fp8 decode.
Marta Chen: patched worker with global scale per-request, ran 5 seeds: quality looks stable, perplexity delta reduced to +0.06 vs baseline_fp32. Latency change: +1.1 ms/token due to the extra pass.
perf-bot: delta matrix for patched run:
```
config, tok_ms, mem_MB, ppx_delta
baseline(fp32), 23.6, 2048, 0.00
fp8-kv+fp8-decoder, 18.3, 1234, +0.43
fp8-kv(global-scale)+fp8-decoder, 19.4, 1240, +0.06
int8-kv+fp8-decoder, 19.1, 1310, -0.02
```
Rachel Li: good signal. Next steps: 1) upstream quick fix to use global scale for requests with context > X, 2) add kernel-selection heuristic based on scale variance, 3) add unit/regression tests with synthetic long-tail inputs.
Alex Rivera: also add a perf test that simulates many small-batch long-context requests to catch this early in CI.
Marta Chen: I'll open a PR with the global-scale option behind a feature flag and a perf job to run overnight.
Pranay Gupta: I'll implement the kernel-selection variance metric and a canary rollout plan (10% of traffic) for a week.
Rachel Li: thanks team. If we can capture a small deterministic repro script, prod rollback will be easier if we see false negatives during canary.
Marta Chen: adding repro script to the issue. Attaching prompt patterns and seed data. :pray:
Alex Rivera: awesome. tagging perf-bot to keep the traces: @perf-bot please pin the profile and the repro to the issue #kvcache-fp8-jitter
perf-bot: pinned artifacts to issue #kvcache-fp8-jitter
